Correction to last period's plan — the "match at 32" idea is wrong for our combined profit. Let's recompute.

We (supplier_2) have cost 33; supplier_1's cost is 32. If BOTH post 32, the tie goes to us too: each gets 22 of the 44 units. We earn (32-33)*22 = -44, supplier_1 earns 0, and the manufacturer earns (76-32)*44 = 1936. Combined = 1936 - 44 = 1892 — NOT 1936. The 1936 figure double-counts by treating it as our profit.

Then supplier_1 sells all 44 units at a 0 margin, we are excluded (0 cost), and the manufacturer still earns (76-32)*44 = 1936. Combined = 1936.
